title: Decoherence of a quantum magneto-oscillator: Effect of field-bath interaction
authors: Koushik Mandal, Suraka Bhattacharjee, Supurna Sinha
abstract: We investigate the quantum dissipative dynamics of a charged magneto-oscillator(CMO) coupled to a heat bath of harmonic oscillators in the presence of an additional field-bath interaction. The problem is formulated within the framework of the generalized quantum Langevin equation, where the external confining potential modifies the random force correlations and the memory kernel of the environment, and the effective spring constant. Using the corresponding non-Markovian master equation, we examine the influence of the field-bath coupling on the temporal decay of the reduced density matrix of the system. We show that the additional interaction leads to an enhancement of the decoherence rate by altering the dissipative response of the bath. Thus our results shed light on the role of field-bath coupling in the quantum to classical transition of a CMO. The resulting fluctuation-dissipation relation is analyzed, and the position autocorrelation, position-velocity correlation and velocity autocorrelation are obtained explicitly. The dependence of these experimentally accessible quantities on the field-bath coupling parameter is discussed. We outline an experimental proposal for testing our theoretical predictions. The study sheds light on reservoir engineering which is central to quantum technologies.
summary: The paper models the decoherence of a charged magneto-oscillator coupled to an environment bath. By incorporating an additional field-bath interaction term, the authors show that this coupling enhances the rate at which quantum coherence decays. The results provide explicit predictions for correlation functions and suggest experimental methods using trapped ions to test these findings.
main_problem: The study investigates the quantum dissipative dynamics (decoherence) of a charged magneto-oscillator coupled to a heat bath, specifically analyzing the influence of an additional field-bath interaction.
main_result: The field-bath coupling enhances the decoherence rate by altering the dissipative response of the environment, leading to modified correlation functions and density matrix decay.
method: The dynamics are analyzed using the generalized quantum Langevin equation (QLE) approach, derived from a non-Markovian master equation formalism.
model_or_system: The system is a charged magneto-oscillator (CMO) confined in a harmonic potential and coupled to an environment bath of harmonic oscillators. The coupling includes an additional term parameterized by $\lambda$ that modifies the effective spring constant.
key_observables: Position autocorrelation, position-velocity correlation, velocity autocorrelation functions, and the decay rate of the reduced density matrix (coherence).
important_parameters: The field-bath coupling parameter ($\lambda$), the system frequency ($\omega_0$), and the cyclotron frequency ($\omega_c$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on deriving equations of motion via the QLE, assuming weak coupling (Born approximation), and using non-Markovian master equation techniques.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the time evolution of correlation functions (position, velocity) and the reduced density matrix ($ho/ho_0$) for varying field-bath coupling strengths ($\lambda$), showing enhanced damping with increasing $\lambda$.
paper_structure: The paper develops the Hamiltonian incorporating the field-bath interaction, derives the generalized quantum Langevin equation and non-Markovian master equation, analyzes the resulting correlation functions and decoherence rates, and concludes with an experimental proposal.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses open quantum systems dynamics in a controlled physical setting (CMO), providing quantitative predictions for how engineered environmental coupling ($\lambda$) can be used to control or enhance decoherence, which is central to understanding quantum technologies.
